03/Dated: 09.08.2024 Prayer 1.

This writ petition has been filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India for the following reliefs:-
(a) For issuance of an appropriate order(s) and/or direction(s) for setting aside the order dated 20th of February 2024 (Annexure-10), 15th of December 2023 (Annexure-8) and 17th of July 2023 (Annexure-7) passed in LA Case No. 4 of 2005 by the Ld. Court of Senior Civil Judge-II, Dumka wherein the prayer made by the Petitioner to mark the original sale deed bearing number 3234 of 84 as an exhibit has been rejected.

(b) For issuance of an appropriate order(s) or direction(s) under the Ld. Court Senior Civil Judge-II, Dumka to mark the original sale deed bearing number 3234 of 84 as Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
1
an exhibit in LA Case No. 4 of 2005.
(c) For issuance of an appropriate writ(s), order(s) or direction(s) to stay the proceedings with respect to LA Case No. 4 of 2005 till the pendency of the instant application.
Facts 2.

The brief facts of the case, as per the pleading made in the petition, read as under:-
3.

It is the case of the plaintiff/petitioner that the petitioner is plaintiff in LA Case No.4 of 2005,
while the respondents are the contesting defendants in LA Case No.4 of 2005.
4.

It is the further case of the petitioner that the land located within Mouza Baliya, Thana No.2,
appertaining to Khata No.32, Plot No.53 and 53/187 admeasuring an area of 21 bighas 11 Khatas and 7 Dhurs was acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Land Acquisition Case was registered as LA case No.54 of 2001-2002.
5. The award was prepared in the name of the petitioner, however, the same was contested by the respondents who claimed right, title and interest on the suit property.

6. The Divisional Commissioner, Santhal Pargana Division, Dumka, vide its order dated 10th May,
2005 passed in Rev. Misc. Appeal No.46/2004-2005 had issued direction upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dumka to refer the matter to the court below as the case involved complicated questions of law and fact.

In pursuant to the reference made by the Deputy Commissioner, Dumka,
two separate LA Case being LA case No.4 of 2005 and LA Case No.5 of 2005 were registered, for the purpose of determination to whom the compensation will be payable.
7. The petitioner filed his written statement/show cause, wherein, it has been stated that the respondents were strangers and had no concern with the land.
Thereafter, the written statement cum claim was filed by the respondents, wherein, it was stated that they are the descendants of the then Zamindar, namely, Raja Kamleshwar Prasad Singh.

8. During the pendency of the LA Case being LA Case No.4 of 2005, the petitioner filed an application on 3rd June, 2023, wherein, the petitioner prayed the leave of the court to file certain documents including the original sale deed bearing no.3234 of 1984, certified copy of the order passed in mutation case no.48/94-95 and the certified copy of the deposition of P.W. 1 in LA Case No.5 of 2005.

The learned court has allowed the application dated 3rd June, 2023 vide order dated 4th July, 2023 and granted the leave to the petitioner to file the same documents subject to payment of cost of Rs.600/-
9.

After obtaining the leave of the court, the petitioner filed all the documents along with the application, thereafter, the learned court vide order dated 17.07.2023 was pleased to mark certified copy of the order passed in mutation case no.48/94-95 and the certified copy of the deposition of Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
2 PW 1 in LA Case No.5 of 2005 as exhibit 1 and 2.
The learned court however, declined to mark the sale deed bearing no.3234 of 1984 as an exhibit.
10. The petitioner renewed its prayer vide application dated 30.08.2023.
The learned court vide order dated 15.12.2023 was pleased to reject the same by reiterating the findings of the order dated 17.07.2023.

The petitioner again filed an application dated 06.01.2024 for the same relief as referred above but the learned court vide order 20.02.2024 was pleased to reject the application in the light of orders dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023.
11.

It is evident from the factual aspect that in the suit, the sale deed was sought to be exhibited and for which, the petitions were filed twice, which were rejected vide orders dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023.
Subsequent to the said rejection, again a petition has been filed on 06.01.2024 praying the same relief of marking exhibit of the said sale deed.
12. The defendants had appeared and made serious objection by raising the issue that the aforesaid prayer has already been rejected twice vide orders dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023.
As such, said order having been accepted, hence, the fresh petition, i.e., petition dated 06.01.2024 ought not to have been filed.

13. The learned Court, agreed with the said contention, has rejected the petition dated 06.01.2024,
vide order dated 20.02.2024, which is impugned along with order dated 15th of December 2023)
and 17th of July 2023 by filing this petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
Argument of the petitioner 14.

Mr. Prashant Pallav, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted by admitting the fact that earlier for the same relief, the petition was rejected, i.e., vide order dated 17.07.2023 after marking the other documents as exhibit, save and except, sale deed no.3234 of 1984.
15.

It has been contended that the learned court ought to have been taken into consideration, in the ends of justice, while rejecting the petition dated 06.01.2024 that even though, the said prayer was rejected on 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023 but for doing the substantial justice, the petition dated 06.01.2024 ought to have been allowed.
Analysis 16.
This Court has heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and appreciated the argument advanced on his behalf.

17. The admitted fact herein is that the document which has been sought to be exhibited, i.e., the sale deed which was brought on record and so far as the issue of marking of exhibit is concerned, the prayer was twice rejected on 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023.
18.

But it is the admitted fact that the petitioner has not challenged the order dated 17.07.2023 or 15.12.2023, rather, after waiting, has made an application for again seeking the same prayer for Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
3 marking the exhibit.

The same has been rejected by the trial court after taking into consideration that earlier on two occasion petition was filed for the same cause which has already been rejected vide orders dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023.
19.

The contention has been raised that both the orders, i.e., 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023 have also been challenged in this proceeding along with the rejection of the petition dated 06.01.2024 vide order dated 20.02.2024.
20.

The question which requires consideration by this Court:
"As to whether, the prayer which has been sought for in the petition dated 06.01.2024, the subject matter of the present petition, has been rejected twice vide orders dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023, hence, after accepting the same, the prayer can again be allowed to be made by the petitioner for marking the said document as an exhibit."
21.

The second question which also requires consideration by this Court:
"Whether in a petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, the earlier order can also be allowed to be challenged by making the three prayers."
22.

This Court, needs to consider the second question regarding the issue of entertaining the petition on the ground of assailing the three orders which has been passed on the same cause of action, i.e., orders dated 17.07.2023, 15.12.2023 and 20.02.2024.
23.

It needs to refer herein that the order can be allowed to be challenged together if the order is of the authority of the different hierarchy, which is in a case, i.e., if the order has been passed after the stages of three hierarchy, i.e., Original, Appellate and the Superior Authority or the Court of law,
then the merger of principle will apply and in that circumstances, only one order, i.e., if the order passed by the final forum will be challenged, then it will suffice, reason being that, if the final order will be quashed by the court of law or the higher forum, then all the previous orders will stand quashed on the principle that the moment, the higher forum will pass an order concurring with the view of the original or the appellate authority, then, in the law, it will be presumed that the order passed by the original and the appellate authority are having no existence.

24. The aforesaid aspect of the matter has been taken into consideration by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala, (2000) 6 SCC 359, in particular at paragraph 7, 8, 12 and 42, which reads as under:
"7.

entities.text: Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala, (2000) 6 SCC 359
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctrine of merger is neither a doctrine of constitutional law nor a doctrine statutorily recognised.
It is a common law doctrine founded on principles of propriety in the hierarchy of justice delivery system.
On more occasions than one this Court had an opportunity of dealing with the doctrine of merger.

It would be advisable to trace and set out the judicial opinion of this Court as it has progressed through the Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
4 times.

8. In CIT v. Amritlal Bhogilal and Co.1 this Court held:
"There can be no doubt that, if an appeal is provided against an order passed by a tribunal, the decision of the appellate authority is the operative decision in law.

entities.text: CIT v. Amritlal Bhogilal and Co.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the appellate authority modifies or reverses the decision of the tribunal, it is obvious that it is the appellate decision that is effective and can be enforced.
In law the position would be just the same even if the appellate decision merely confirms the decision of the tribunal.

As a result of the confirmation or affirmance of the decision of the tribunal by the appellate authority the original decision merges in the appellate decision and it is the appellate decision alone which subsists and is operative and capable of enforcement;"
12.
The logic underlying the doctrine of merger is that there cannot be more than one decree or operative orders governing the same subject-matter at a given point of time.

When a decree or order passed by an inferior court, tribunal or authority was subjected to a remedy available under the law before a superior forum then, though the decree or order under challenge continues to be effective and binding, nevertheless its finality is put in jeopardy.

Once the superior court has disposed of the lis before it either way -- whether the decree or order under appeal is set aside or modified or simply confirmed, it is the decree or order of the superior court, tribunal or authority which is the final,
binding and operative decree or order wherein merges the decree or order passed by the court,
tribunal or the authority below.
However, the doctrine is not of universal or unlimited application.

Merger in law is defined as the absorption of a thing of lesser importance by a greater, whereby the lesser ceases to exist, but the greater is not increased; an absorption or swallowing up so as to involve a loss of identity and individuality."

25. The decision in Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala (Supra) was followed by a three-Judge Bench decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Chandi Prasad v. Jagdish Prasad, reported in (2004) 8 SCC 724,
wherein at paragraphs 23 and 24 it has been held which read hereunder as:-
"23.

entities.text: Chandi Prasad v. Jagdish Prasad, reported in (2004) 8 SCC 724
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctrine of merger is based on the principles of propriety in the hierarchy of the justice delivery system.
The doctrine of merger does not make a distinction between an order of reversal, modification or an order of confirmation passed by the appellate authority.
The said doctrine postulates that there cannot be more than one operative decree governing the same subject-matter at a given point of time.

24. It is trite that when an appellate court passes a decree, the decree of the trial court merges with the decree of the appellate court and even if and subject to any modification that may be made in the appellate decree, the decree of the appellate Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
5 court supersedes the decree of the trial court.
In other words, merger of a decree takes place irrespective of the fact as to whether the appellate court affirms, modifies or reverses the decree passed by the trial court."

26. This Court, applying the aforesaid principle in the facts of the present case, has found that it is not a case of the petitioner that the order dated 17.07.2023 and order dated 15.12.2023 have been passed by the different hierarchical court, rather, by the same court, thus, it is evident that principle of merger cannot be applied in the facts of instant case.

27. It requires to refer herein the settled proposition of law that if the order passed by the concerned court has not been challenged by the party concerned before the higher forum, it amounts that party concerned has accepted the said order which has been passed by the court of competent jurisdiction.
28. In the instant case the petitioner has filed the petitions thrice with the same prayer and the learned trial court has rejected the same all the time.

29. Further, It is apparent from the record that the same court has already applied its mind and the earlier the petition which was filed with the same prayer has been rejected and the same has not been challenged by the petitioner before the appellate court rather petitioner has filed a fresh petition on 06.01.2024 with the same prayer before the same court.

30. The Court has considered the jurisdiction that once the decision has already been passed by the same Court, i.e., vide order dated 17.07.2023 and 15.12.2023, then, on the principle, the court is having no power to recall its order unless provided under the statute.

31. It cannot be disputed that the concerned trial court is having no jurisdiction to recall its order and if in those circumstances, the learned trial court has passed an order rejecting the petition dated 06.01.2024 on the ground that the said issue has already been considered and rejected by the court being the same issue, which according to the considered view of this Court, cannot be said to suffer from an error.
32.

The matter would be considered to be not in accordance with law if the learned trial court would have allowed the petition dated 06.01.2024 and in that circumstance, it will be considered to be exceeding the jurisdiction by the learned trial court.

33. This Court is conscious with the fact that this Court is exercising the power conferred under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, wherein, the principle applies that only in case of jurisdictional error or error apparent on the face of record, the interference is to be shown by the Court exercising the power conferred under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, reference in this regard may be made to the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shalini Shyam Shetty

Vrs. Rajendra Shankar Patii, reported in (2010) 8 SCC 329, wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down the scope of Article 227 which relates to the supervisory powers of the High Courts and by taking aid of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Full Bench of Calcutta High Court in the case of Dalmia Jain Airways Ltd. Vrs. Sukumar Mukherjee, reported in AIR 1951 Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
6 Calcutta 193, wherein, it has been laid down that Article 227 of the Constitution of India does not vest the High Court with limit less power which may be exercised at the court's discretion to remove the hardship of particular decisions.

entities.text: Dalmia Jain Airways Ltd. Vrs. Sukumar Mukherjee, reported in AIR 1951 Catholic Diocese
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The power of superintendence confers power of a known and well recognized character and should be exercised on those judicial principles which give it its character.

In general words, the High Court's power of superintendence is a power to keep the subordinate courts within the bounds of the authority, to see that they do what their duty requires and that they do it in a legal manner.

i. The power of superintendence is not to be exercised unless there has been;
(a) An unwarranted assumption of jurisdiction, not vested in a court or tribunal; or (b) gross abuse of jurisdiction; or (c) an unjustifiable refusal to exercise jurisdiction vested in courts or tribunals.

ii. Further, in the aforesaid judgment the Hon'ble Apex Court has taken aid of a judgment rendered in the case of Mani Nariman Daruwala Vrs. Phiroz N. Bhatena, reported in (1991) 3 SCC 141,
wherein it has been laid down that in exercise of jurisdiction under Article 227, the High Court can set aside or reverse finding of an inferior court or tribunal only in a case where there is no evidence or where no reasonable person could possibly have come to the conclusion which the court or tribunal has come to.

entities.text: Mani Nariman Daruwala Vrs. Phiroz N. Bhatena, reported in (1991) 3 SCC 141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: iii. The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that except to this limited extent the High court has no jurisdiction to interfere with the finding of facts.

iv. Further, the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Laxmikant Revchand Bhojwani Vrs. Pratapsing Mohansingh Pardeshi, reported in (1995) 6 SCC 576 it has been laid down that the High Court under Article 227 cannot assume unlimited prerogative to correct all species of hardship or wrong decisions.

entities.text: Laxmikant Revchand Bhojwani Vrs. Pratapsing Mohansingh Pardeshi, reported in (1995) 6 SCC 576
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Its exercise must be restricted to grave dereliction of duty and flagrant abuse of fundamental principles of law and justice.
v. It has been laid down at paragraph 47 of the aforesaid judgment that the jurisdiction under Article 227 is not original nor is it appellable.
This jurisdiction of superintendence under Article 227 is for both administrative and judicial superintendence.
Therefore, the powers conferred under Article 226 and 227 are separate and distinct and operate in different fields.

Another distinction between these two jurisdictions is that under Article 226 the High Court normal annuls or quashes an order or proceedings but in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 227, the High Court, apart from annulling the proceeding, can also substitute the impugned order by the order which the inferior tribunal should have made.
vi.
It has further been laid down regarding the powers to be exercised by the High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.

The High Court, in exercise of its jurisdiction of superintendence, can interfere in order only to keep the tribunals and courts subordinate to it Catholic Diocese Through Its Current ... vs Radhe Chand Lal Choudhary Aged About Not ... on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55940395/
7 within the bounds of its authority, in order to ensure that law is followed by such tribunals and courts by exercising jurisdiction which is vested with them and by not declining to exercise the jurisdiction which is vested in them.

Apart from that, High Court can interfere in exercise of its power of superintendence when there has been a patent perversity in the orders of the tribunals and courts subordinate to it or where there has been a gross and manifest failure of justice or the basic principles of natural justice have been flouted.

vii. In exercise of its power of superintendence High Court cannot interfere to correct mere errors of law or fact or just because another view than the one taken by the tribunals or courts subordinate to it, is a possible view.
In other words the jurisdiction has to be very sparingly exercised.

34. It is evident from the judgment as has been referred hereinabove that the Court exercising the supervisory power as under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, is only to see error apparent on the face of record or if the order has been passed without any jurisdiction.

35. This Court, on the basis of discussion made hereinabove, and particularly taken into consideration that the learned trial court has rejected the petition dated 06.01.2024 vide order dated 20.02.2024, on the ground that earlier on two occasions, the said issue has already been considered and rejected by the court, is of the view that the order dated 20.02.2024 passed by the learned trial court, cannot be said to suffer from an error.
36.
Accordingly, this petition fails and is dismissed.
37. Pending Interlocutory Application(s), if any, stands disposed of.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, A.C.J.) Rohit/-A.F.R.
